elements.element: Customer is not contractually prohibited from soliciting Vendor personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 affirmatively provides that Customer may solicit any Vendor employee.

elements.element: Customer is prohibited from soliciting Vendor personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 permits Customer to solicit any Vendor employee and imposes no non-solicitation obligation.

elements.element: Vendor is prohibited from soliciting Customer personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: No operative language imposes a non-solicitation obligation on Vendor.

elements.element: Covered personnel are limited to personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause establishes no covered-personnel category or direct-involvement limitation.

elements.element: The 12-month period begins when each covered person's involvement in the Services ends.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no end-of-involvement trigger.

elements.element: General advertisements are carved out from the mutual non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 protects Customer hiring arising from general recruitment, but no mutual carve-out applicable to both parties is stated.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are carved out from the mutual non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: No operative language expressly addresses unsolicited approaches or provides a mutual carve-out.

elements.element: Neither party is subject to a no-hire or no-employment restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly permits Customer to hire or employ any Vendor employee, Section 12.3 disclaims a Customer no-hire commitment, and no restriction is imposed on Vendor hiring Customer personnel.

result.reason: The redline fully achieves the preferred position by replacing Customer's non-solicitation restriction with an express permission to solicit. It does not implement the fallback because it creates no mutual, personnel-limited, 12-month non-solicit, although it does preserve the required absence of a no-hire restriction. The change is confined to the targeted restriction and is consistent with Section 12.3.
